text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Estonian and Finnish representatives initialled an agreement on visa-free travel between the two countries from May 1. The official accord is to be signed on March 26.
- NATO deputy secretary general Sergio Balanzino reassured the Baltic states at an international security conference that the doors of NATO will not close after the first round of enlargement.
- President Lennart Meri presented 27 orders, medals and badges of merit.
- Estonian and Ukrainian Prime Ministers Tiit Vaehi and Pavlo Lazarenko discussed cooperation opportunities and how to increase mutual investments during Vahi's visit to Ukraine.
- Parliament discussed a draft law on amending the law on foreign relations, which would increase the role of the government and parliament and reduce that of the president and the foreign ministry.
- MP Arvo Junti, a former Development Party member, will form his own party.
- A joint Estonian-Latvian army exercise will be held in the end of February, early March in southern Estonia.
- Potential candidate for premier, Mart Siimann, can rely on a certain majority of votes but has failed to widen the coalition as right-wing parties refuse to co-operate.
- Formerly loss-making investment funds have managed to make a significant profit in six months and their yield is generally higher than that of shares.
- The finance ministry is to decide next week on recommendations to cut income tax to 15 percent.
- A regular source of income for parliament members are fees for articles published in the press.
